title: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment.
paragraphs: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment.
Morning light touches the edge of the camp as Abraham places bread and a waterskin into Hagar’s hands… and the silence feels heavy.

This is not a triumphant moment.
It is complicated. Painful. Human.
I watch Ishmael glance back once… as if searching for something familiar before the long road begins.
And yet… even in this painful separation, God’s promise has not disappeared.
Sometimes the story of faith includes moments we don’t fully understand—choices that ache, paths that divide, promises that unfold in ways no one expected.
Standing there as a witness, I realize something quietly powerful:
God did not forget Ishmael in the wilderness.
Even complicated promises still hold grace.
And maybe that truth still speaks today…
For the places in our lives where the story feels unfinished… or difficult to explain.
Because even in the wilderness… God still hears.
I am only a witness to this moment, quietly observing the story unfold.
💭 What part of this moment moves you the most—the goodbye, the uncertainty, or the quiet hope ahead?
